items.label: Studio Areas
items.notes: Select six courses from at least four of the following studio areas. At least one must be designated with an A.

items.label: Art History Elective
items.notes: Select one course from the following course or range:

nodes.title: Drawing
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; five hours arranged. Course in basic drawing skills intended as preparation for work in variety of media. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Sculpture
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; five hours arranged. Introduction to concepts and forms of contemporary sculpture to become familiar with tools and material to enable students to visually manifest their individual ideas. Presentation of work of contemporary artists. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Painting
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; five hours arranged. Basics of painting: introduction to technical procedures, tools, and materials. Discussion of fundamental conceptual and formal concerns. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Photography
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; five hours arranged. Fundamentals in technique, with emphasis on individual projects. Varied approaches, processes, and applications of photographic medium within context of art, supported by studies in theory, aesthetics, and history of photography. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Printmaking
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; five hours arranged. Introductory survey of various technical and conceptual concerns in variety of printmaking media as preparation for more focused study in particular media at upper-division level. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: New Genres
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; five hours arranged. Introduction to projects in installation, performance, video, film, intermedia, and other nontraditional media and processes. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Ceramics
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; five hours arranged. Introduction to ceramic materials and processes, with emphasis on personal and cultural expression in ceramic media. Discussion of ceramics in contemporary artistic practice and social history of ceramic art. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Rise of Modernism in Global Context
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; field trips, three hours. Examination of global forces underlying development of modernist thought on art and society from mid-19th through early-20th centuries. Exploration of origins, development, theory, and practice of modernism in context of colonialism and industrialization. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Global Modernism
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; field trips, three hours. Art majors should complete courses 31A, 31B, and 31C in sequence in first year. Continuation of impact of modernist ideas through mid-20th century, with focus primarily on work made from 1920s to 1960s globally. Examination of how modernist ideas and practices were influenced by industrialization, urbanization, colonialism, world wars, and emancipatory movements. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Modernism and Its Discontents
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; field trips, three hours. Art majors should complete courses 31A, 31B, and 31C in sequence in first year. Continued impact of modernist ideas from 1960s to present, covering shift from modernist to postmodernist practices and theories. Examination of critiques of modernism drawing from emancipatory movements and poststructuralist, feminist, queer, performance, postcolonial, and critical race theory. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Drawing
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Drawing as both independent expressive medium and as means of visualization. May be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Drawing: Topics in Anti-Racism, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Varied approaches to drawing media and content to develop students' technical, expressive, and conceptual tools to understand and explore anti-racism, equity, diversity, and inclusion. Combination of courses 130 and 130A may be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Survey of Critical Thought
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; screenings/research, 11 hours. Overview of premodern, modern, and postmodern theory as reflected in critical writing and artistic frameworks from late 19th century to present. Introduction to elements of Marxism, critical theory, feminist and queer theory, indigenous critique, disability studies, black radical tradition, decolonial and postcolonial writings. Specific topics may vary. May be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Painting
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Varied media and subjects to further develop students’ technical and expressive means to implement their ideas. May be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Painting: Topics in Anti-Racism, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Varied approaches to painting media and content to develop students’ technical, expressive, and conceptual tools to understand and explore anti-racism, equity, diversity, and inclusion. Combination of courses 133 and 133A may be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced New Genres
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Emphasis to be selected by faculty members from one or more of following media: installation, performance, video, film, other nontraditional media and processes. May be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced New Genre: Topics in Anti-Racism, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Varied approaches to new genres media and content to develop students’ technical, expressive, and conceptual tools to understand and explore anti-racism, equity, diversity, and inclusion. Combination of courses 137 and 137A may be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Printmaking
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Selected studies in fine printmaking, historical and contemporary: woodcut, etching and engraving, lithography, silk screen, mixed media. May be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Sculpture
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Selected studies in sculpture, historical and contemporary: modeling, carving, casting, welding, and other media; forms in space, including installations and nonstudio pieces. May be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Sculpture: Topics in Anti-Racism, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Varied approaches to historical and contemporary sculpture that highlights its social impact and cultural content. Themed lectures and studio assignments develop students’ technical, expressive, and conceptual tools to understand and explore anti-racism, equity, diversity, and inclusion as expressed in objects, sculpture, and built environment. Combination of courses 145 and 145A may be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Photography
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Selected projects in photography and related media, concentrating on development of individual students’ artwork. Studio emphasis with special topics in theory and critical analysis. May be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Photography: Topics in Anti-Racism, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Varied approaches to photography’s history, media, and content to develop students’ technical, expressive, and conceptual tools to understand and explore anti-racism, equity, diversity, and inclusion. Combination of courses 147 and 147A may be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Ceramics
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Selected studies in ceramics, with emphasis on individualized creative experimentation with materials and techniques introduced in course. Methods and processes to be selected from range of possibilities, including handforming and modeling, preparation and use of molds, slipcasting, and use of potter’s wheel. May be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Ceramics: Topics in Anti-Racism, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Varied approaches to clay media and content to develop students’ technical, expressive, and conceptual tools to understand and explore anti-racism, equity, diversity, and inclusion. Combination of courses 148 and 148A may be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Interdisciplinary Studio
nodes.description: Studio, six hours; discussion, one hour; nine hours arranged. Varied project-based studies in conceptually-driven approaches to art making in which students’ core concerns and aims determine all aspects of projects, including medium, method, and presentational context. Combination of courses 149 and 149A may be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Interdisciplinary Studio: Topics in Anti-Racism, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
nodes.description: Studio, six hours; discussion, one hour; eight hours arranged. Varied project-based studies in conceptually-driven approaches to art making that advance anti-racism, equity, diversity, and inclusion. Students’ core concerns and aims determine all aspects of projects, including medium, method, and presentational context. Combination of courses 149 and 149A may be repeated for maximum of 20 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Senior Capstone
nodes.description: Studio, eight hours; seven hours arranged. Limited to senior Art majors. Advanced senior projects and portfolio development, with emphasis on analysis and criticism of individual creative work and ideas. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Chicana Art and Artists
nodes.description: (Same as Chicana/o and Central American Studies M175 and World Arts and Cultures M128.) Lecture, four hours. Introduction to Chicana art and artists. Examination of Chicana aesthetic. Chicana artists have developed unique experience and identity as artists and Chicanas. Letter grading.
